paper_title: Anisotropic cosmic optical background bound for decaying dark matter in light of the LORRI anomaly
notes: Limit from Fig. 3 (ALP2-crop.pdf in the e-print), the 95% CL exclusion on the ALP-photon coupling g_chi-gamma-gamma for ALP dark matter (R=1, q_gamma=2) derived from the HST cosmic optical background anisotropy. The figure shows two 'this work' regions (HST 0.606 um and HST 0.85 um); the 0.606 um bound is the stronger of the two at all masses 5-30 eV, so the reported envelope coincides with the HST 0.606 um curve. Boundary coordinates recovered from the vector paths of the filled exclusion regions; axes calibrated from tick labels (x linear 5-30 eV, y log 1e-12 to 5e-10 GeV^-1). The paper defines Gamma = g^2 m^3 / (64 pi) (Eq. decayrate), i.e. the standard L = -(g/4) a F Ftilde convention, so no conversion was needed. Cosmological (mean cosmic DM density) bound, not a local-halo search, so no rho_DM rescaling applied. Cross-check: the curve corresponds to Gamma ~ 2e-24 s^-1 at 10 eV, consistent with the abstract's quoted 1e-24 to 1e-23 s^-1 exclusion over 5-20 eV.
